q: Every Monday at 9:00 forty analysts open the same dashboards and queries sit in the queue. Each query is fast once it starts. What should you change?
o: Increase the warehouse size from Small to Large
Increase the maximum number of clusters
Turn off Photon
Lower the auto stop timeout
e: Queueing means not enough concurrent capacity. More clusters (scale out) run more queries at the same time; a bigger size only makes each query faster.

q: One complex query spills to disk in the query profile and takes 20 minutes. Nobody else uses the warehouse. What is the most direct fix?
o: Add more clusters
Enable the result cache
Use a bigger warehouse size
Switch to a classic warehouse
e: A single query runs on one cluster. Spill shows the cluster has too little memory for it, so more compute per cluster (scale up) helps.

q: You run the same query twice on a SQL warehouse, but between the runs someone inserts rows into the table. What happens to the second run?
o: It is computed again, because the table changed
It returns the cached result from the first run
It fails until the cache is cleared
It returns the cached result plus the new rows
e: The query result cache is invalidated when the underlying tables change, so the warehouse recomputes the result.

q: What mainly drives the cost of a SQL warehouse?
o: The number of queries run
The number of rows returned
The number of users with CAN USE
Its DBU rate (size and clusters) multiplied by the time it is running
e: You pay DBUs for the time clusters are up, whether busy or idle. That is why auto stop and right-sizing matter most.

q: Why can a serverless warehouse use a much shorter auto stop than a pro warehouse without annoying users?
o: Serverless warehouses never stop
Serverless starts in seconds, so a restart is barely noticed
Pro warehouses do not support auto stop
Serverless keeps the disk cache after stopping
e: Pro and classic machines take minutes to start in your cloud account. Serverless compute is ready in seconds, so stopping early saves money with little impact.
